It did NOT check origin/grok/v2-natq-20260903, where the entire lineage lives. My later 'no SYSTEM-H runner on any branch' claim repeated the same omission, covering three refs rather than all five. Both statements were wrong because the search space was wrong, not because the artifacts were absent.
recovery_standard: All artifacts exist as git blobs with verifiable SHA256, independent of any conversational summary. Two independent copies agree: the git object store and a detached worktree at 37adc2c.

discrepancy.severity: blocks the NATQ-002 preregistration as written
authoritative_sources: EVAL-NATQ-VAL-001 preregistration and REPORT, where it was recomputed and verified OK
discrepancy.finding: 3fade96a appears ONLY on my own branch. It is a hash minted over my own SYSTEM-H record during the earlier freeze; it is not the upstream identity and never was. The NATQ-002 preregistration therefore pins an identity that does not correspond to the authoritative frozen SYSTEM-H.
discrepancy.consequence: Recovering the artifacts does NOT by itself unblock the NATQ-002 run. Even with every original in hand, executing against the current preregistration would verify against the wrong hash. A coordinator decision is required first.

second.claim_in_my_natq002_preregistration: SYSTEM-H has never been scored on any benchmark
second.evidence: EVAL-NATQ-VAL-001 scored SYSTEM-H on the frozen NATQ-001 validation set, n=40, 53 gold spans, with SYSTEM_H_config_hash 7599eb3c recomputed and verified OK, holdout not opened.
second.why_this_matters: My preregistration justified its paired design on the grounds that no prior anchor existed. A prior anchor DOES exist. The paired design remains sound, but its stated rationale was wrong — and more importantly the approved case_hit@10 PASS floor of 0.80 sits far above SYSTEM-H's known 0.50 case-level result on a comparable natural-query validation set. On that evidence SYSTEM-H would likely FAIL the approved floor. The coordinator should see this BEFORE authorising a run, not after.
second.metric_caveat: EVAL-NATQ-VAL-001's strict_recall_at_10 and my case_hit@10 are similar but not proven identical in definition. The comparison is indicative, not exact.
